summary: Face recognition can now be set up from the app, with a button. THE DEAD END: enrolling a photo on a host without the models failed with 'face models are not installed - run the face-recognition setup to download them'. Every word of that was true and it was useless: the setup it named was ai/setup.ps1 -Faces, a PowerShell script in the source tree, which is not a thing to tell somebody standing in a browser trying to enrol a face. AN ERROR WITHOUT A ROUTE TO THE FIX IS A HALF-BUILT FEATURE. New services/face_models_install.go (FaceModelsInstaller) + three routes on the faces API: GET /api/faces/models says what the host still needs, POST /api/faces/models/install starts a background job, and /install/status streams its log - the same shape as the ffmpeg and AI-runtime installers. It fetches ONLY what is missing (the common real state is 'detector present, recognizer missing', because the export face-blur already uses YuNet), pip-installs opencv-python when the detector's interpreter lacks the FaceDetectorYN/FaceRecognizerSF classes - a host can have both models and still fail, which is a DIFFERENT repair and the status says which one is needed - and then LOADS both models with the real cv2 calls the worker makes, because a file of the right size is not proof it is the right file. The directory is checked writable BEFORE the download: 37 MB is a long way to travel to learn the destination is read-only. checkFaceModelFile rejects the two ways this download succeeds and is still not a model, both arriving as a valid 200: a git-LFS pointer (a ~130-byte text stub GitHub serves for LFS-tracked files through some URL forms - named explicitly, because 'too small' would send somebody to look at their network instead of the URL) and a truncated transfer. The UI is one component in two places: a panel on the People screen that appears the moment the page loads, so the operator is told BEFORE picking a photo rather than by a failure after, and the SAME control in Settings > AI beside the AI-runtime installer, where it also shows the ready state. A rejected enrolment re-checks the host, so the message and the button that fixes it arrive together. The page's live-state line is SUPPRESSED while setup is outstanding - a green 'Recognizing 1 person on 2 cameras' under a banner saying the models are missing is the screen contradicting itself. ALSO FIXED, found by the bench data rather than by reading: rebuildGallery exported a zero-length faceprint straight to the worker, and the worker builds one matrix per person with np.asarray(embeddings), which raises on a ragged list inside a try that wraps the WHOLE gallery load - so ONE malformed row did not degrade one person, it aborted the load and NOBODY was recognized on ANY camera, with a single line on the worker's stderr as the only symptom. The export now drops empty and odd-length vectors (what a truncated write and a model change respectively leave behind) and says so in the log. Verified live end to end on a throwaway instance: the banner listed exactly the one missing 37 MB file, the button downloaded it (38,696,353 bytes - a real file, not an LFS stub), the banner disappeared, and three photos then enrolled through the REAL file picker at 88% quality with their face crops on screen and three 128-d faceprints in the gallery the worker reads. `.install-output` also got its first stylesheet rule - the AI-runtime installer's pip log had been rendering as an unstyled <pre> that grew without bound.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no config change and no schema change. THREE NEW ROUTES under /api/faces, admin-only by the same catalog row as the rest of that surface (the permission matrix denies by default, so viewer and operator get 403 without a new rule). The install needs outbound HTTPS to github.com; there is no bundled copy and no mirror, so an air-gapped appliance still uses ai/setup.ps1 -Faces on a connected machine and a file copy - the panel names the folder to copy into. Model files remain .gitignore'd and are never committed. Nothing needs restarting after an install: the embedder checks for the files per call and the live worker reloads when the gallery is rebuilt on the next enrolment. The gallery-export guard changes what is WRITTEN to faces_gallery.json, not what is stored: a malformed embedding row stays in the database and is skipped on export, so an install that had one now recognizes everybody else instead of nobody. services.DetectorCommandFromConfig is newly exported (was the private detectorCommand on PythonInstaller); no behaviour change for existing callers. Frontend adds 19 dictionary keys in en/ms/zh/ar and a new manual section (#setup) on the People page in all four languages.
